assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bark is the outer covering of a tree that acts as its protective layer.

copy.en: Bark is the outer covering of a tree that acts as its protective layer.
copy.tl: Ang balat ng puno (bark) ay ang panlabas na takip nito na nagsisilbing proteksyon sa punongkahoy.
copy.bis: Ang panit sa kahoy (bark) mao ang gawas nga tabon niini nga nanalipod sa kahoy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A barnacle's cement is so strong it sticks permanently
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions strength of barnacle cement, which is a physical property, but it does not teach describing physical properties of solid materials like hard, shiny, or stretchable. copy.en:
How strong is barnacle glue?

A barnacle's cement is so strong it sticks permanently — even underwater in the open sea!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalakas ang pandikit ng barnacle?

Napakalakas ng pandikit ng barnacle kaya kumakapit ito nang permanente, kahit nasa ilalim ng tubig-dagat!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka kusog ang pandikit sa barnacle?

Hilabihan ka kusog ang pandikit sa barnacle nga mopilit kini og permanente, bisan ilawom sa tubig-dagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Barnacles have a special body part called a cement gland that makes and releases their sticky glue.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an internal gland that produces glue, not an outer body part (head, legs, wings) nor a role in movement or food gathering. It shares the topic of animal body parts but does not support the competency's specific skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Barnacles have a special body part called a cement gland that makes and releases their sticky glue.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a body part that produces adhesive, but does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it provide an example of adaptation like mimicry or camouflage. It is only tangentially related to animal adaptations.

copy.en: Barnacles have a special body part called a cement gland that makes and releases their sticky glue.
copy.tl: May espesyal na bahagi ang barnacle na tinatawag na cement gland, ito ang gumagawa at naglalabas ng kanyang pandikit.
copy.bis: Ang barnacle adunay espesyal nga bahin sa lawas nga gitawag og cement gland nga mohimo ug mopagawas sa iyang pandikit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its super glue also works on wood, metal, plastic, and glass, even underwater.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes barnacle glue's ability to stick to various surfaces, not the physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It shares the topic of materials but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A barnacle doesn't stick only to rocks — its super glue also works on wood, metal, plastic, and glass, even underwater.
copy.tl: Hindi lang sa bato dumidikit ang barnacle — gumagana rin ang pandikit nito sa kahoy, metal, plastik, at salamin, kahit nasa ilalim ng tubig.
copy.bis: Dili lang sa bato mopilit ang barnacle — molihok usab ang iyang pandikit sa kahoy, metal, plastik, ug salamin, bisan ilawom sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The barnacle's hard shell is made of calcium carbonate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a barnacle's shell, an outer body part, but does not describe its role in movement or food gathering as required by the competency. It only states the shell's material composition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The barnacle's hard shell is made of calcium carbonate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the shell is hard, a physical property, but the competency requires describing physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not describe the property itself; it only identifies the material (calcium carbonate) and notes it is tough. It does not teach the concept of physical properties of solids.

copy.en:
What is a barnacle's hard shell made of?

The barnacle's hard shell is made of calcium carbonate — the very same tough material found in seashells and chalk!
copy.tl:
Ano ang gawa sa matigas na balat ng barnacle?

Ang matigas na balat ng barnacle ay gawa sa calcium carbonate — ang parehong matigas na sangkap na makikita sa mga kabibi at sa chalk!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gama sa gahi nga kabhang sa barnacle?

Ang gahi nga kabhang sa barnacle hinimo sa calcium carbonate — ang samang gahi nga sangkap nga makita sa mga kabibi ug sa chalk!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A barnacle's hard shell is made of plates like a little wall, with tiny plates on top that open and close like a door.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the barnacle's shell plates, which are outer body parts, but it does not describe parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor does it identify their role in movement or gathering food. The opening/closing action is not tied to the competency's required functions.

copy.en: A barnacle's hard shell is made of plates like a little wall, with tiny plates on top that open and close like a door.
copy.tl: Ang matigas na balat ng barnacle ay gawa sa mga plato na parang pader, may munting plato sa taas na bumubukas at sumasara na parang pinto.
copy.bis: Ang gahi nga balay sa barnacle hinimo sa mga plato nga sama sa paril, adunay gagmayng plato sa ibabaw nga muabli ug musira sama sa pultahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A young barnacle actually swims freely in the sea at first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the barnacle lives in the sea (aquatic habitat), but it does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine animals/plants by habitat, nor does it teach classification. The habitat reference is incidental, not instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A young barnacle actually swims freely in the sea at first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: G5-L-6 requires comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants. The card describes a barnacle's larval swimming stage, which is not one of the specified groups (mammals, birds, plants). It does not support comparing those life cycles.

copy.en:
Did barnacles always stay in one place?

A young barnacle actually swims freely in the sea at first — then it picks a spot and glues itself down for life!
copy.tl:
Naglalangoy ba muna ang barnacle bago tumigil sa isang lugar?

Ang batang barnacle ay lumalangoy muna nang malaya sa dagat, bago ito pumili ng lugar at dumikit doon habambuhay.
copy.bis:
Molangoy ba una ang barnacle sa dili pa kini mopuyo permanente?

Ang batan-ong barnacle molangoy una nga libre sa dagat, sa dili pa kini mopili og dapit ug mopilit didto hangtod sa kahangtoran.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It eats tiny bits floating in the water and is just hitching a ride to reach food-rich water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: Hitchhiking without eating the whale is not competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It eats tiny bits floating in the water and is just hitching a ride to reach food-rich water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: A hitchhiking filter-feeder is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
Does a barnacle eat the whale it rides on?

Many think a barnacle eats the whale it clings to — but usually it does NOT! It eats tiny bits floating in the water and is just hitching a ride to reach food-rich water.
copy.tl:
Kinakain ba ng barnacle ang whale na sinasakyan nito?

Maraming akala kinakain ng barnacle ang whale na kinakapitan nito — pero karaniwang HINDI! Kumakain ito ng maliliit na lumulutang sa tubig at nakikisakay lang para makarating sa tubig na maraming pagkain.
copy.bis:
Ginakaon ba sa barnacle ang balyena nga iyang gisakyan?

Daghan ang naghunahuna nga gikaon sa barnacle ang balyena nga iyang gikuptan — apan kasagaran DILI! Mokaon kini og gagmay nga naglutaw sa tubig ug nagsakay lang aron makaabot sa tubig nga puno og pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a barnacle stays in that exact same spot for its entire life
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about barnacle behavior (never moving after attachment), not about classifying Philippine animals/plants by habitat using a drawing or diagram. It does not support the competency's required classification activity or format.

copy.en:
Does a barnacle ever move again?

Nope! Once it glues itself down, a barnacle stays in that exact same spot for its entire life.
copy.tl:
Gumagalaw pa ba ang barnacle?

Hindi na! Kapag dumikit na ito, mananatili ang barnacle sa iisang lugar habang buhay.
copy.bis:
Molihok pa ba ang barnacle?

Dili na! Kon mopilit na kini, magpabilin ang barnacle sa usa ka dapit sa tibuok kinabuhi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A barrier reef lies farther from the shore! It is separated from the land by a deep, calm lagoon of water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a barrier reef and lagoon, which are natural landforms/bodies of water, but it does not identify local examples of the listed landforms (mountains, valleys, rivers, coastlines) nor describe how they influence living and non-living components. It only states a geographic fact about barrier reefs, providing no direct instructional support for the competency's action.

copy.en: A barrier reef lies farther from the shore! It is separated from the land by a deep, calm lagoon of water.
copy.tl: Ang barrier reef ay nasa mas malayo sa baybayin! Hinihiwalay ito ng lupa sa pamamagitan ng isang lagoon o lawa ng tubig.
copy.bis: Ang barrier reef anaa sa mas layo gikan sa baybayon! Nabulag kini gikan sa yuta pinaagi sa usa ka lagoon o lawa sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They can hear ultrasound up to about 100,000 Hz
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a frequency value (100,000 Hz) but does not describe wave properties using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity, nor does it involve research from secondary sources. It is a specific fact about bat hearing, not instruction on wave property terminology.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They can hear ultrasound up to about 100,000 Hz
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about hearing ultrasound, which relates to sound, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It provides a factual hearing range for bats, not an exploration of sound production or transfer.

copy.en: Bats have amazing ears! They can hear ultrasound up to about 100,000 Hz, which they use for echolocation.
copy.tl: Nakakapakinig ang mga paniki ng ultrasound na umaabot sa mga 100,000 Hz, na ginagamit nila para sa echolocation!
copy.bis: Ang kabog makadungog og ultrasound hangtod mga 100,000 Hz, nga ilang gigamit alang sa echolocation!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it sends out clicks super fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a bat's echolocation clicks, which is a specialized animal behavior, not an everyday situation like a ringing bell or hearing noises. It does not directly teach how sound is made or transferred in everyday contexts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it sends out clicks super fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a bat using sound for echolocation, not about sources and uses of sound energy at school, home, or in the local community. It does not support the competency's focus on everyday energy sources and uses.

copy.en:
What is a bat's 'feeding buzz'?

When a bat closes in on an insect, it sends out clicks super fast, almost blurring together — called a feeding buzz. More clicks mean more info on exactly where the prey is.
copy.tl:
Ano ang 'feeding buzz' ng paniki?

Kapag papalapit na ang paniki sa insekto, mas pinapabilis nito ang mga klik hanggang halos magsanib — tinatawag itong 'feeding buzz.' Mas maraming klik, mas eksaktong nalalaman kung nasaan ang biktima.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang 'feeding buzz' sa kabog?

Kung hapit na ang kabog sa insekto, iyang padaghanon ang klik hangtod hapit na magtapok — gitawag kining 'feeding buzz.' Mas daghang klik, mas eksakto nga mahibaw-an asa gyud ang biktima.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why can't we hear a bat's loud calls?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a bat's call is inaudible to humans (pitch too high) and why it must be loud (faint echo). It does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations; it focuses on sound properties (loudness, pitch) rather than the mechanism of sound production or transmission.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pitch is too high
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions pitch (frequency) but does not use scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity to describe wave properties. It does not involve research from secondary sources or systematic description of wave properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the echo from a tiny insect is so faint
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies sound travels from a source (bat) to a receiver (insect) and back, but it does not explicitly identify that waves carry energy from a source to a receiver. The focus is on loudness and pitch, not on energy transfer by waves.

copy.en:
Why can't we hear a bat's loud calls?

A bat's call is louder than a person shouting! We just can't hear it because the pitch is too high — it must be loud since the echo from a tiny insect is so faint.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi natin naririnig ang malakas na tili ng paniki?

Ang tili ng paniki pala ay mas malakas pa sa sigaw ng tao! Hindi lang natin ito naririnig dahil sobrang taas ng tono nito — kailangan itong malakas dahil mahina ang alingawngaw mula sa maliit na insekto.
copy.bis:
Nganong dili nato madungog ang kusog nga tingog sa kabog?

Ang tingog sa kabog diay mas kusog pa sa singgit sa tawo! Dili lang nato kini madungog kay sobra kataas ang tono niini — kinahanglan kining kusog kay luya ang alingawngaw gikan sa gamay nga insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A bat's feet are built to grip without effort
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific adaptation of bat feet for hanging, not the general outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement or gathering food. It does not directly support observing/describing body parts for locomotion or feeding.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its own body weight pulls tendons that lock the claws shut
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a structural adaptation (locking tendons) that helps bats hang, but it does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment through mimicry or camouflage, nor does it use secondary sources. It is a related example of adaptation but not the specific competency.

copy.en: A bat's feet are built to grip without effort — its own body weight pulls tendons that lock the claws shut, so it never falls, even asleep!
copy.tl: Ang paa ng paniki ay nakadisenyo para kumapit nang hindi napapagod — ang bigat ng katawan nito ang humihila sa litid na nagsasara ng mga kuko, kaya hindi ito nahuhulog kahit natutulog!
copy.bis: Ang tiil sa kabog gidisenyo aron mokapyot nga walay kakapoy — ang kabug-aton sa lawas niini ang mobira sa ugat nga mosira sa mga kuko, mao nga dili kini mahulog bisan natulog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hunters like snakes or ground animals can't easily reach bats when they're hooked to a high cave ceiling or branch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hunters like snakes or ground animals can't easily reach bats
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not an example of mimicry or camouflage as animals changed to better suit their environment.

copy.en:
Why do bats hang upside down so high up?

For safety! Hunters like snakes or ground animals can't easily reach bats when they're hooked to a high cave ceiling or branch.
copy.tl:
Bakit nakabitin nang mataas ang mga paniki?

Para sa kaligtasan! Hindi madaling maabot ng mga mangangaso tulad ng ahas o hayop sa lupa ang paniki kapag nakasabit ito sa mataas na kisame ng kweba o sanga.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagbitay man og habog ang mga paniki?

Alang sa kaluwasan! Dili dali maabot sa mga tigpangayam sama sa bitin o hayop sa yuta ang paniki kon nagsangit kini sa habog nga kisame sa langub o sanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many bats sleep hanging upside-down from cave ceilings all day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bats and a cave habitat but does not use a drawing or diagram to classify animals by terrestrial/aquatic/aerial habitat, nor does it present any classification scheme. It only states a behavioral fact about bats.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: then come out only at night to feed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes nocturnal roosting behavior but does not describe how bats have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. No adaptation or evolutionary change is explained.

copy.en: Many bats sleep hanging upside-down from cave ceilings all day, then come out only at night to feed!
copy.tl: Maraming paniki ang natutulog na nakabitin sa kisame ng kuweba kapag araw, at lumalabas lang sa gabi para kumain!
copy.bis: Daghang kabog ang matulog nga nagbitay sa atop sa langob panahon sa adlaw, ug mogawas lang sa gabii aron mokaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its energy comes from a cool chemical reaction happening right between the electrodes and the electrolyte!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a chemical reaction occurs inside a battery; it does not explain bond formation/breaking or the formation of a new substance, which is the core of G9-M-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its energy comes from a cool chemical reaction happening right between the electrodes and the electrolyte!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that chemical reactions may be exothermic or endothermic
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a chemical reaction but does not identify it as exothermic or endothermic, nor does it discuss heat energy changes. The word 'cool' is colloquial and not a scientific claim about energy transfer.

copy.en: Where does a battery get its power? Its energy comes from a cool chemical reaction happening right between the electrodes and the electrolyte!
copy.tl: Saan nagmumula ang enerhiya ng baterya? Galing ito sa isang chemical reaction na nangyayari sa pagitan ng electrodes at ng electrolyte!
copy.bis: Asa naggikan ang enerhiya sa baterya? Gikan kini sa usa ka chemical reaction nga nahitabo tali sa electrodes ug sa electrolyte!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A battery goes dead when nearly all the chemicals inside it have been completely used up by the chemical reaction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a chemical reaction consuming chemicals, but it does not explain bond formation/breaking or the formation of a new substance, which is the core of G9-M-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A battery goes dead when nearly all the chemicals inside it have been completely used up by the chemical reaction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example involving a chemical reaction but does not address reversibility of physical changes or irreversibility of chemical changes, which is the required competency.

copy.en:
Why does a battery go dead?

A battery goes dead when nearly all the chemicals inside it have been completely used up by the chemical reaction!
copy.tl:
Bakit nauubos ang baterya?

Nauubos ang baterya kapag halos lahat na ng chemicals sa loob nito ay nagamit na nang paulit-ulit sa chemical reaction!
copy.bis:
Nganong mahurot ang baterya?

Mahurot ang baterya kon halos tanan nga chemicals sa sulod niini magamit na sa chemical reaction!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each charge and use slightly damages the materials inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes battery wear and loss of energy capacity but does not explain physical versus chemical changes or reversibility/irreversibility. The idea of damage is only loosely connected to chemical change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each charge and use slightly damages the materials inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions materials being damaged but does not describe chemical properties such as burning, reacting, or degradability/biodegradability. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A rechargeable battery gets weaker over time! Each charge and use slightly damages the materials inside, so after hundreds of charges, it holds less energy than when it was new.
copy.tl: Humihina ang rechargeable na baterya habang tumatagal! Unti-unting nasisira ng bawat charge ang mga sangkap sa loob, kaya pagkatapos ng daan-daang beses, hindi na ito humahawak ng kasing-daming enerhiya.
copy.bis: Maluya ang rechargeable nga baterya samtang molabay ang panahon! Hinay-hinay nga makadaot sa materyales sa sulod ang matag pag-charge, busa human sa gatusan ka beses, dili na kini makakupot sa daghan nga enerhiya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The bayawak basks in sunlight to warm up its body before it becomes active.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a current behavioral adaptation (basking) but does not describe how animals have changed over time to suit their environment, nor does it use secondary sources. It is only tangentially related to adaptation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because it's cold-blooded! The bayawak basks in sunlight to warm up its body before it becomes active.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a behavior related to being cold-blooded, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Basking is a response to temperature, but the card does not frame it as a general characteristic of living things or teach the competency's content.

copy.en:
Why does a bayawak sunbathe?

Because it's cold-blooded! The bayawak basks in sunlight to warm up its body before it becomes active.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagpapainit sa araw ang bayawak?

Dahil cold-blooded siya! Nagpapainit ang bayawak sa sikat ng araw para tumaas ang temperatura ng katawan bago mag-aktibo.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagpainit sa adlaw ang bayawak?

Tungod kay cold-blooded siya! Nagpainit ang bayawak sa sinag sa adlaw aron mopataas ang temperatura sa lawas ayha mag-aktibo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Beaufort scale has 13 levels!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card provides a specific fact about the Beaufort wind scale (13 levels, Force 0–12). The competency asks students to identify basic weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, etc. The card does not teach how to identify or describe wind speed as a weather characteristic; it only states the number of levels in a scale. This is peripheral vocabulary about wind speed, not direct instructional support for identifying weather characteristics.

copy.en: The Beaufort scale has 13 levels! It goes from Force 0 (calm, no wind) to Force 12 (hurricane force).
copy.tl: Ang Beaufort scale ay may 13 antas! Mula Force 0 (kalmado, walang hangin) hanggang Force 12 (lakas ng bagyo).
copy.bis: Ang Beaufort scale adunay 13 ka lebel! Gikan sa Force 0 (kalma, walay hangin) ngadto sa Force 12 (kakusog sa bagyo).

Gawas sa waggle dance ug kompas sa adlaw, ang mga bubuyog nagmemorya usab og mga landmark palibot sa ilang puyo aron makabalik human sa taas nga paglakbay.

A worker bee's stinger has tiny barbs that get stuck in your skin—when it pulls away, part of its body tears off, and it dies.

May maliliit na kawit ang tibod ng bubuyog na natitirik sa balat—kapag humila ito palayo, napupunit ang bahagi ng katawan nito at namamatay.

Ngano nga mamatay ang buyog human motusok?

Adunay gagmayng kawit ang tuslok sa buyog nga mahigot sa panit—kon mobira kini palayo, magisi ang bahin sa lawas niini ug mamatay.

A honeybee's stinger has tiny barbs, so it stays stuck in the skin — and the bee dies after stinging just once.

Ang tibo ng pukyutan ay may maliliit na kawit, kaya naiiwan ito sa balat — at namamatay ang pukyutan pagkatapos manuot nang isang beses lang.

Ang tusok sa putyokan adunay gagmayng tunok, mao nga mabilin kini sa panit — ug mamatay ang putyokan human makasundot og makausa ra.

Beeswax comes straight from a bee's own body — it oozes out as tiny flakes from under its belly to build the comb.

Ang pagkit na ginagamit ng bubuyog sa paggawa ng bahay-pukyutan ay galing mismo sa katawan nito — lumalabas ito bilang maliliit na piraso mula sa ilalim ng tiyan.

Ang talo nga gigamit sa putyukan sa pagtukod og balay gikan mismo sa lawas niini — mogawas kini isip gagmay nga piraso gikan sa ilawom sa tiyan.

A bee's eyes catch fast movement quicker than ours do. Even flowers swaying in the wind still look clear and sharp to a bee, so it's very hard to catch one off guard.

Bakit hirap kang gulatin ang bubuyog?

Mas mabilis nakikita ng mata ng bubuyog ang mabilis na galaw kaysa sa atin. Kahit umuuga ang bulaklak sa hangin, malinaw pa rin itong nakikita nila, kaya mahirap silang gulatin.

Mas paspas makita sa mata sa putyokan ang paspas nga lihok kaysa kanato. Bisan giuyog sa hangin ang bulak, klaro gihapon kini nakita sa putyokan, mao nga lisod sila hadlokon.

Ang beetles o salagubang! Mas marami ang uri o species nito kaysa sa kahit anong grupo ng hayop sa mundo.
